Question Choices: How many lines of symmetry does a square have? Enter only the number.
Hints: Count two midlines and two diagonals.|Each fold maps the square onto itself.
Solution: A square has four reflection axes: two lines joining opposite side midpoints and its two diagonals. Each reflects the entire square onto itself.

Question Choices: Select. How many lines of symmetry does a circle have? ~~Infinitely many | 0 | 2~~
Hints: Every diameter is a fold line.|There is no limit to their number.
Solution: Every line through the center reflects a circle onto itself. There are infinitely many possible directions for such lines, so there are infinitely many symmetry axes.

Question Choices: How many lines of symmetry does a scalene triangle have? Enter only the number.
Hints: All sides have different lengths.|No fold matches the halves.
Solution: A reflection symmetry of a triangle would fix one vertex and exchange the other two, forcing the two sides from that fixed vertex to be equal. A scalene triangle has three different side lengths, so it has no reflection symmetry.

Question Choices: What is the smallest positive rotation that maps a regular hexagon onto itself about its center? Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Hints: Its rotational symmetry has order 6.|Divide 360 by 6.
Solution: The regular polygon has 6 equally spaced vertices. The smallest matching turn advances one vertex position, so its angle is 360/6 = 60 degrees.

Question Choices: Select. Does a parallelogram that is not a rectangle or rhombus have any line of symmetry? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Try folding along midlines and diagonals.|None match the halves.
Solution: No. A reflection symmetry of a parallelogram would require either the rectangle case (right angles) or the rhombus case (equal adjacent sides). Both are excluded here. It still has half-turn rotational symmetry.
